name: Contemporary Art Platform (CAP)
funding: Private non-profit founded 2011 by Amer Al-Huneidi; shows co-hosted with the Lebanese Business Council, Tanmia charity and UNHCR (2024)

name: Dar al-Athar al-Islamiyyah
funding: Manages the al-Sabah Collection, on permanent loan to Kuwait under its National Council for Culture, Arts and Letters. Sponsors: KIPCO, Kuwait Petroleum Corporation and subsidiaries, Kuwait Finance House.

name: Bishkek School of Contemporary Art (BiSCA)
funding: Founders built its online school at no cost, per 24.kg (2020). Asia Art Archive is a partner on Mobile Library: Kyrgyzstan, April 2025 to June 2026. No funder list found.

name: Gapar Aitiev Kyrgyz National Museum of Fine Arts
Kim? Contemporary Art Centre
funding: Latvian Ministry of Culture, State Culture Capital Foundation, Riga City Council, Altum and EU social-entrepreneurship co-financing; project supporters KRASO, Kokmuiža and Media Port.

name: Latvian National Museum of Art
funding: State-funded museum under Latvia's Ministry of Culture. Its 2025 show Light from Italy was backed by the Italian Embassy, Riga City Council, Rietumu Banka and the ministry.

name: Riga International Biennial of Contemporary Art (RIBOCA)
funding: Private. Founded by Agniya Mirgorodskaya, daughter of Russian fishing businessman Gennady Mirgorodsky. The organisers said funding moved to a US charity, Just A Moment, after 2022.

name: Arab Image Foundation (AIF)
funding: Stichting DOEN, Gerda Henkel Stiftung, Culture Resource Mawred and Hillman Family Foundations are listed as supporters on its site.

name: Ashkal Alwan
funding: Small NGO. Major benefactors: Robert A. Matta Association, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Andy Warhol Foundation, Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Teiger Foundation; Sfeir Semler Gallery is a patron.

name: Beirut Art Center (BAC)
funding: Independent non-profit foundation, cultural grants, community patrons; zero commercial gallery sales.

name: Arete Foundation for Arts and Culture
funding: Small non-profit founded 2012 by Reem Gibriel, Khaled Mattawa and Nedal Swehli; AFAC grants in 2012, 2016 and 2019 (NACP National Fund).
